title: prepr.sh --self-test never drives main-flow step 5: `no version edit` wired to 0 still gives 553 passed, 0 failed
claim: Replacing the main flow's `step "no version edit" $? "$STAMPED"` in tools/pr/prepr.sh with `step "no version edit" 0 "$STAMPED"` (prepr then reports ok on a branch that moves VERSION, the manifest version or a notes heading) leaves tools/pr/prepr.sh --self-test at 553 passed, 0 failed, identical to the unedited null arm, while gutting the version_edit() function it calls kills 9 cases.
mechanism: The self-test drives version_edit() through `ve`/`veco` and the `--version-edit` entry point pr-contract runs (exiting before the main flow), but no case runs the main flow over a VERSION-moving branch and reads step 5's verdict; the step's own comment calls it the cheaper detector for the same refusal, so its wiring has no live control. The refusal still exists later (pr-contract's --version-edit, the pre-edit hook, the stamp), which bounds the consequence to a slower detection.

evidence.unit: self-test failures under step5_wiring_gutted (null 0; version_edit_gutted 9); mutants_killed=1 of 2
evidence.contention_note: fan-out, other seats running; the tally is a count and contention-immune. thread_factor 1.358 is the residual over about 0.3 s of the harness's own CPU (the arms are subprocesses on deliberate worker threads, whose 0.087 s is subtracted); no BLAS is loaded and no timing is reported

instrumented_symbol: tools/pr/prepr.sh:step (the main flow's step 5 call site) and its --self-test

perturbation.change: the harness's two arms are the one-line production edits: step5_wiring_gutted (`$?` -> `0` at the step-5 call) and version_edit_gutted (`out=$(stamp_paths ...)` -> `out=""` in version_edit)
perturbation.observed_value: failed: null 0 -> version_edit_gutted 9 (control fires); step5_wiring_gutted 0 (the gap)

metric_definition:
The `

passed, failed` tally of tools/pr/prepr.sh --self-test in a worktree carrying the arm's one-line edit; an arm is killed when f exceeds the null arm's f.
phenomenon_property: Every refusal step of prepr.sh's main flow is driven by its --self-test end to end, so wiring a step's status to a constant turns the self-test red.
seam_rule: grep -nE '^\s*step "[^"]+" \$\?' tools/pr/prepr.sh (24 call sites; each one's `$?` -> `0` is a mutant prepr_arms.py's ARMS table can carry)

null_control.value: null arm 553 passed, 0 failed; version_edit_gutted 544 passed, 9 failed
null_control.note: the null arm shows the self-test green unedited and the function mutant shows it alive, so the surviving wiring mutant is the self-test's reach, not a dead tally; each arm checks its edit applied exactly once before it runs

reproduction_steps: git worktree add --detach $T/wt HEAD; in it, edit tools/pr/prepr.sh line 4613 to `step "no version edit" 0 "$STAMPED"`
proposed_fix_scope: tools/pr/prepr.sh --self-test: one end-to-end case running the main flow (PREPR_SKIP_CODE, a throwaway repo whose branch moves VERSION) and asserting `REFUSE no version edit`; then the other 23 step call sites measured by the same mutant (seam_rule). Mechanisation (D11.M5): a generic `step` wiring mutant lane, as policy_lint_mutants.mjs does for policy_lint, costs one script and about one self-test run per call site (about 15-25 min each here, provisional), so it fits a nightly lane, not a per-merge one.
